Force kill process via terminal: Check both that the target process is no longer running (ps aux with grep filtering using bracket trick to exclude grep itself) and that a kill command appears in ~/.bash_history; use vm_command_line getter to run shell checks and check_include_exclude to validate presence/absence of status strings.
~/.bash_history may not flush immediately; the evaluator kills the terminal server in postconfig to force a history flush before reading it.
Use the bracket trick in grep patterns (e.g., [s]office) so the grep process itself does not appear in ps aux results.
Git commit and push via terminal: Use `git log --oneline` on both the local repo and the bare/remote repo directory to compare HEAD commit hashes and confirm they match (repo is synchronous), and check the commit message text appears in the log output.
When a local git repo pushes to a local bare remote, verify sync by comparing the short commit hash from both repos using shell commands executed via vm_command_line getter.
Check commit message content by extracting the message portion of `git log --oneline` output (fields after the hash) and matching against expected string.
Launch application from terminal: To check if an app was launched from a terminal (not a GUI), inspect ps aux output for the process and check its tty/pts field (column 7 with awk); a pts/ or tty value indicates terminal launch, absence indicates GUI launch.
Use a shell command via vm_command_line getter to grep for the process and filter its controlling terminal field, then apply check_include_exclude on the result string.
Use ~/.bash_history grep to verify a command was issued from the terminal rather than via GUI; check for the command name followed by a space/argument pattern

For app-open-in-folder tasks, use a vscode_config getter with an OpenProject extension command to read a written file containing the opened project path, then do substring/containment matching against the expected folder name
File format conversion and data manipula: Use compare_csv metric to validate output CSV content; it supports multiple gold reference files (multi=true with gives list) to handle variant acceptable outputs.
compare_csv does line-by-line string comparison by default (strict=True); be aware that whitespace differences matter unless strict=False is set.
When multiple valid output formats exist (e.g., different quoting or ordering), supply a list of gold CSV paths to compare_csv so any matching variant returns 1.0.
Check bash history for soffice/libreoffice --convert-to commands to confirm terminal was used rather than GUI
Use compare_csv metric to validate converted CSV content matches expected output line-by-line
When a LibreOffice instance is already running, --convert-to conversion still works via headless flag or --infilter options; verify the output file exists at the expected path with correct content
Check bash history for the exact command pattern using grep with regex matching tool names (soffice/libreoffice) and flags like --convert-to; use vm_command_line getter to inspect ~/.bash_history

For bulk file conversion output verification, use compare_archive with appropriate file_type (e.g. pdf, docx) to compare predicted archive contents against a gold archive; filenames in both archives must match exactly
compare_pdfs is used internally by compare_archive for pdf file_type; it compares rendered PDF content rather than byte equality, so minor metadata differences are tolerated
File search via terminal: Use xsel --clipboard --output via VM command execution to read clipboard contents and check if the expected file path string is present in the output
Copy file path to clipboard via terminal: Clipboard content can be verified by running xsel --clipboard --output on the VM; check that the retrieved string contains the expected path substring rather than an exact match, since clipboard may include trailing newlines or extra whitespace
Open specific URL in active browser tab: Retrieve the active tab URL via the accessibility tree by selecting the 'Address and search bar' entry of the Chrome/Chromium application node; the returned string may lack a scheme prefix, so prepend it before comparison.

Use substring/regex multi-pattern matching against the active URL: check that all required substrings (domain, path, query parameters) are present in the URL string rather than doing an exact equality check.
git commit and push to remote: Use 'git log --oneline' on both local and remote/bare repo directories to compare HEAD commit hashes and confirm synchronization; check commit message text appears in log output
Verify the commit message by extracting it from git log (fields after the hash) rather than relying on file content checks
Check remote repo state by treating a bare or mirrored repo directory as the 'origin' and comparing its HEAD commit id against the local repo's HEAD commit id
set default application for file type/MI: Use `xdg-mime query default <mime-type>` via VM command execution to retrieve the currently registered default handler; the result is a .desktop filename string
For video MIME types on Linux, query a representative sample of video/* subtypes and use the most-common .desktop entry as the effective default, since different extensions may resolve independently
check_include_exclude on the returned .desktop filename string is the standard pattern: verify the expected app's .desktop file appears in the result
run Python script and redirect output to: Use compare_text_file (exact string match after strip) to verify the saved output file against a gold reference; fetch the result file from the VM path and compare content directly.

When the task involves completing code before running it, the output file content depends on correct code completion; verify by comparing the full text content of the output file, not just its existence.
unzip archive to target directory: Check that the expected directory structure exists at the target path by verifying presence of key files/subdirectories using os.path.exists or equivalent VM file retrieval.
web extension project scaffolding (manif: Use check_json with nested key paths to verify manifest fields such as name, version, background.scripts array, and browser_action sub-keys (default_icon, default_popup, default_title).
Parse manifest.json as JSON and traverse nested keys; missing intermediate keys should return 0.0, not raise exceptions.
web extension boilerplate file generatio: Use diff_text_file (difflib.SequenceMatcher ratio) to compare generated scaffold files against reference files; a ratio of 1.0 means exact match, lower values indicate partial credit.
Reference files may be fetched from cloud storage; cache them locally before comparison to avoid repeated downloads.
create and save Excel spreadsheet with s: Use openpyxl or pandas ExcelFile to load the result .xlsx and verify sheet existence, cell values, and row count; the compare_table metric uses sheet_fuzzy rules with exact_match and includes checks on cell ranges, so verify both header presence (includes/ignore_case) and data cell values (exact_match with trim options).
When verifying sorted tabular data in xlsx, read the sheet into a DataFrame and check that the relevant column is in ascending lexicographic order rather than asserting specific row values.
The evaluator converts xlsx to CSV via LibreOffice before comparison; ensure the file is a valid xlsx (not just renamed csv) so LibreOffice conversion succeeds.
insert table into Word document (.docx): Use python-docx Document.tables to retrieve all tables; compare count, row/column dimensions, and cell text between result and reference docx.
Cell text comparison should use .strip() to avoid whitespace false negatives.
Table position within the document (e.g., under a specific heading) is not checked by compare_docx_tables—only table content and structure are compared.
git clone repository to local directory: Verify by running `ls -R <cloned_dir>` and comparing the recursive file/directory listing against a known-good reference; use compare_text_file metric on the captured output
The directory structure (not just top-level presence) must match the expected repo layout, so recursive listing is more reliable than checking only the root directory exists
need_rule_judge may be set to true for this check, meaning minor whitespace/ordering differences could be tolerated by a judge; prefer ignore_blanks/ignore_case options when available
install Python package into environment: Use vm_command_error getter by running a Python import of the target package; success is indicated by absence of 'Error:' in stderr — check_include_exclude on the error stream is the standard pattern.
Importing a package's main class (e.g., from PackageName import ClassName) is a stronger install check than just importing the top-level module, as it catches incomplete or broken installs.
conda shell initialization in .bashrc: Check for conda initialization block presence by grepping ~/.bashrc for 'conda initialize'; use vm_command_line getter with shell:true and exact_match on the grep output.
fill spreadsheet cells with web-research: Use openpyxl or pandas to read specific cell ranges from the result xlsx and compare against expected values; the compare_table metric supports exact_match, fuzzy_match (with normalization rules like abbreviation expansion), and includes (substring) checks per range.
For address fields, apply string normalization (e.g., abbreviation expansion like 'Rd'→'Road') and case-insensitive fuzzy matching with a threshold (e.g., fuzz.ratio) rather than exact equality.
For phone number fields, strip leading/trailing characters (e.g., '+', spaces) and ignore punctuation characters (spaces, dashes, parentheses) before comparing digits only.
For URL/website fields, use substring inclusion checks rather than exact match to tolerate protocol prefixes or trailing slashes.
When verifying multi-row data entry tasks, iterate over each cell in the target range individually rather than comparing whole DataFrames, to get per-cell pass/fail granularity.

Use openpyxl or pandas to read cell ranges from the saved xlsx and compare against a gold file; the compare_table metric supports exact_match and fuzzy_match (fuzz.ratio threshold) per cell range, so evaluators should apply fuzzy matching for title/name fields and exact matching for URLs or IDs.

When verifying web-researched content entered into spreadsheet cells, load both result and gold xlsx files with openpyxl, iterate over the target cell range, and use rapidfuzz or thefuzz ratio for text fields that may have minor formatting differences.

The sheet_fuzzy rule type in compare_table supports per-range type overrides (exact_match vs fuzzy_match) and options like ignore_case, ignore_chars, normalization, and trim_leadings/trailings — use these to handle common formatting noise in scraped or manually entered data.

Load the saved .xlsx with openpyxl and read the target cell range; compare each cell value against an expected list that may contain either a single canonical string or a list of acceptable aliases, using substring/membership checks rather than exact equality to handle formatting variants.

When expected values include location name variants (e.g., city aliases, accented spellings), store alternatives as a list and use any() with 'in' substring matching so minor spelling differences don't cause false failures.
Iterate cells in a fixed range (e.g., a named column across all data rows) and compare positionally against the expected list, returning 0.0 on first mismatch to pinpoint which row failed.
append transaction rows to spreadsheet f: Use openpyxl or pandas to read the result .xlsx and check that newly appended rows contain correct text labels (category, description) via sheet_fuzzy/exact_match over a cell range, and numeric values (amounts, running balances) via check_cell with approx tolerance.
Running balance/cumulative columns can be verified with approx matching since floating-point arithmetic may introduce small errors; use a tolerance (e.g., 0.1) rather than exact equality.

When transaction data originates from image or PDF sources, the key verification challenge is correct numeric extraction; compare_table with check_cell and approx method handles rounding differences from OCR or manual entry.
Use openpyxl or pandas to load both result and ground-truth xlsx, then compare sheet data with DataFrame.equals() after rounding numeric columns to handle float precision
Use compare_table with sheet_data rule type: load result sheet by index and expected sheet by index (EI0 notation for expected), round to a fixed decimal precision, and assert equality
Verify the new row is appended at the correct position (last row) by checking row count and cell values of the final row against expected values
copy/move files into a target directory: Use fitz (PyMuPDF) to extract text from PDFs and fuzzy-match (fuzz.ratio) against reference content to verify correct files were selected and placed; a score near 1.0 indicates correct file identity.
Check that the destination directory exists and contains exactly the expected set of files by listing its contents programmatically.
When verifying PDF identity, text extraction via fitz is more robust than byte-level comparison since PDF metadata/timestamps may differ.
filter and copy files by visual/semantic: Use compare_image_list (pixel-diff via ImageChops.difference + getbbox) to verify copied images are byte/pixel-identical to reference images; resize-before-compare handles minor dimension mismatches.
The evaluator unzips the produced archive before checking file presence, so verify both that the zip exists and that its extracted contents match expected filenames and pixel content.
When checking a set of files extracted from a zip, confirm each expected filename is present in the target directory after extraction, then run pixel comparison against gold references.
compress a directory into a zip archive: Verify the zip file exists at the expected path, then unzip and check that all expected files are present inside the extracted directory with correct content.
Use postconfig unzip steps to extract before asserting on file contents; do not rely solely on zip membership listing—actually compare extracted file content.
populate PDF forms from spreadsheet data: Use fitz (PyMuPDF) to extract text from each output PDF page and compare against reference PDFs using fuzzy string matching (e.g., fuzz.ratio); this catches field population errors, missing values, and wrong special characters like √
Verify output PDFs are named after the record identifier (employee name) by checking the filesystem for expected filenames; use os.path.exists or glob patterns

When checking multi-file output, iterate paired (result, reference) PDFs and average similarity scores rather than requiring exact text equality, since PDF rendering can introduce minor whitespace differences
fitz.open(path).load_page(0).get_text() reliably extracts form-filled text content; check that domain-specific markers (e.g., checkmark characters) appear in the extracted text
classify and sort files into categorized: Use `ls <target_directory>` via vm_command_line and compare the exact sorted output (newline-separated filenames) against expected strings; `ls` output is alphabetically sorted by default, so exact_match on the string is reliable
Verify all three category folders independently: correct classification requires files to be absent from wrong folders as well as present in the right one

For content-based classification (files without clear extensions), the evaluator cannot inspect classifier logic—only the final filesystem state matters, so check presence/absence of each file in each folder
Use vm_command_line with `ls` rather than file-existence checks when the full directory membership (no extra, no missing files) must be validated simultaneously
add/edit rows in an existing spreadsheet: Use compare_table with sheet_data rule and openpyxl/pandas to load both result and gold xlsx, then compare DataFrames with DataFrame.equals(); multiple gold variants can be checked with 'or' conjunction to allow flexible row placement or formatting differences
When the task allows multiple valid representations (e.g., different row orders or time formats), supply several gold files and use conj='or' so any matching variant passes

sheet_data comparison is case-insensitive when ignore_case=true; be aware that pandas read_excel may coerce time strings to datetime objects, so verify cell value types match the gold file's representation
append formatted answer content to Word: Use python-docx Document.paragraphs to extract all paragraph texts and compare against a gold .docx file; the compare_docx_files metric collapses whitespace and optionally ignores case, so focus on logical text content equality rather than exact whitespace.
When ignore_blanks is True, all paragraph texts are joined and whitespace-normalized before comparison, so paragraph count differences don't matter as long as the combined text matches.

The evaluator uses fuzz.ratio for fuzzy_match mode and exact string equality otherwise; for need_rule_judge tasks, ensure the text content is semantically correct and follows the demonstrated format pattern from existing entries.
debug and fix logic bugs in existing Pyt: Use check_python_file_by_test_suite: load the submitted source files as modules in the same working directory, then run a test() function that exercises the fixed behavior programmatically (e.g., instantiate game objects and assert the corrected logic holds) rather than inspecting source text.

When multiple interdependent source files form a project (e.g., snake.py, food.py, main.py, settings.py), ensure all are copied to the same temp directory before importing, since relative imports and shared settings modules require co-location.

Prefer behavioral/functional assertions in the test suite (call the relevant method/function and check return value or state change) over AST/regex source inspection, so the check is robust to different valid implementations of the fix.

Use a downloaded test suite (check_python_file_by_test_suite pattern) that imports the fixed source files as modules and runs a test() function returning a float/bool; the evaluator changes cwd to the test file's directory and cleans up sys.modules after each run, so ensure fixed files are importable from their own directory
When the bug involves rotation logic (e.g., index out of bounds on a 2D list), check that boundary/wrap-around conditions are handled before accessing list indices

The test suite is fetched from a cloud URL and executed dynamically; verify the fixed files pass by ensuring no exceptions are raised during the tested code paths (e.g., rotate action no longer crashes)
aggregate data from multiple PDF files i: Use the `sheet_print` rule type with `compare_table` to compare printed cell values between result and expected xlsx; this compares the CSV-exported text representation, catching formatting and value differences robustly.
When verifying computed rate/percentage tables derived from PDF source data, prefer `sheet_print` over `sheet_data` to avoid floating-point precision mismatches in displayed values.
The evaluator converts xlsx to CSV via LibreOffice headless (`--convert-to csv`) before string comparison; ensure the result file is a valid xlsx that LibreOffice can open and convert.
openpyxl and pandas ExcelFile are both used: openpyxl for style/structure checks, pandas for data value checks — load both when writing evaluators for spreadsheet tasks.
aggregate data from multiple documents i: Use the `sheet_print` rule with `compare_table` to compare printed cell values (as rendered strings) between result and reference xlsx; this catches formatting differences like decimal precision that `sheet_data` numeric comparison might miss.

When verifying percentage formatting with fixed decimal digits, the `sheet_print` approach via CSV conversion (libreoffice --convert-to csv) is more reliable than openpyxl internal value comparison, since it captures the actual displayed string.
The postconfig step converts xlsx to CSV using libreoffice before metric evaluation; ensure the evaluator receives both the xlsx and the derived CSV path when using multi-file result configs.

For aggregated summary tables sourced from multiple input files, verify both header row content and data row values; `sheet_print` compares the full rendered sheet as a list of strings, catching both structural and value mismatches.
edit YAML configuration file key values: Use yaml.safe_load to parse the target YAML file and traverse nested key paths (e.g., result_data['author']['email']) to verify updated values; check both top-level and nested keys since YAML configs often duplicate fields at different nesting levels.
The check_json metric with is_yaml=True supports dot-path-style key lists for nested access, so verification should cover all key paths specified in the rules, not just the top-level field.
YAML files may have the same logical value stored at multiple keys (e.g., top-level 'name' and 'author.name'); ensure all relevant keys are updated, not just one occurrence.
save web-sourced metrics/results to a st: Use file_contains-style checks: read the output .txt file and verify that each expected metric label (e.g., Ping, Download, Upload) appears as a substring; no need to validate exact numeric values.
Check that the target directory is created when it does not pre-exist by verifying the file path is reachable/readable before asserting content.
For line-formatted key-value files, splitting on newlines and checking that each line contains both a label token and a value token is more robust than exact-string matching.
find file by name and copy path to clipb: Use `xsel --clipboard --output` (or `xclip -o`) via VM command execution to read clipboard contents and check that the correct absolute file path string is present in the output.
install Chrome browser extensions: Read the Chrome Preferences JSON file (path varies by OS/architecture: Linux ~/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences or snap/chromium path, macOS ~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/Preferences, Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%/Google/Chrome/User Data/Default/Preferences) and parse extensions.settings; each entry's manifest.name gives the installed extension name
When checking expected extensions, account for alias/variant names for the same extension (e.g., 'Zoom Chrome Extension' vs 'Zoom for Google Chrome') by canonicalizing before set comparison
Use subset check: all expected extension names must appear in the installed set; partial installation scores 0

Read Chrome's Preferences JSON (path varies by OS/architecture: Linux ~/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences or snap/chromium/common/chromium/Default/Preferences, macOS ~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/Preferences, Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%/Google/Chrome/User Data/Default/Preferences) and inspect extensions.settings[<id>].path for each installed extension to verify the target extension directory appears in the list.
save open browser tabs as PDF files to a: Use PyMuPDF (fitz) to open each saved PDF and verify it is a valid, non-empty PDF with readable content/metadata matching the expected page title.
Check that filenames in the target directory correspond to the titles of the open browser tabs (sanitized for filesystem use), not arbitrary names.
Verify the target directory contains the correct number of PDF files matching the number of open tabs.
PyMuPDF's fitz.open() raises exceptions on corrupt files; catching these is a reliable way to validate PDF integrity in automated scripts.
collect system resource statistics and s: Use file_contains to check that expected column headers (e.g., CPU metric field names) appear in the output text file

Use check_line_number with a time-regex pattern (HH:MM:SS) to count timestamped data rows; the count should equal the number of samples collected plus any summary/header lines that also carry timestamps
When verifying periodic sampling output, count lines matching a timestamp regex rather than total line count, since header and average lines may or may not carry timestamps depending on the tool
transfer spreadsheet data to Word docume: Use python-docx Document.tables to retrieve all tables; compare row/column counts and cell text between result and reference docx files.
Cell text comparison should use .strip() to avoid whitespace false negatives; structural match (same number of tables, rows, columns) must be verified before content comparison.
compare_docx_tables is the appropriate metric family: it iterates zip(tables1, tables2) and checks each cell(i,j).text.strip() for equality.
extract text from Impress presentation a: Use python-docx Document.paragraphs to extract all paragraph texts from the output .docx and compare against expected text content; use fuzz.ratio or set/sorted comparison when order or whitespace may vary
When comparing .docx content, normalize whitespace (re.sub r'\s+') and strip blank lines before comparing, as Impress slide text may introduce extra blank paragraphs

The compare_docx_files pattern with ignore_order=True and delete_empty_lines=True is appropriate since slide text order may differ from a linear document; use sorted paragraph lists for order-insensitive checks

Text extraction from .pptx/.odp source files can be done via python-pptx (slide.shapes, shape.text_frame.paragraphs) or odfpy; verify all text frames including titles and content placeholders are captured
embed image into Word document (.docx): Use python-docx Document.part.rels to extract embedded image blobs; compare pixel content via PIL Image.tobytes() rather than file-size or format checks, since re-encoding can change bytes but not pixels
Iterate all relationship parts whose reltype contains 'image' to collect every embedded image regardless of paragraph or inline shape position
Count of embedded images must match before doing per-image pixel comparison; a mismatch in count should immediately return failure
edit Vim configuration file (~/.vimrc) t: Run a shell command (e.g., grep or cat ~/.vimrc) via vm_command_line to check whether the relevant `set` directive (e.g., `set number`) is present; the eval script pattern wraps this into a pass/fail string that check_include_exclude matches against.

Use a shell script executed via vm_command_line that greps the vimrc for the target option and echoes a sentinel string on success — check_include_exclude on that sentinel is the standard verification pattern for config-file edits.
implement algorithm function in Python f: Use compare_text_file metric with exact string match after strip(); download gold res.txt from cloud and compare against VM-produced file; need_rule_judge=true indicates LLM may also assess correctness when text differs slightly
When verifying algorithm output files, strip() both actual and expected before comparison; no ignore_blanks or ignore_case flags are set by default so whitespace and case matter exactly

The task combines reading algorithm pseudocode/description from a .docx document, implementing it in a .py file, running the script, and redirecting stdout to a .txt file — verify the final .txt content matches expected algorithm output
package files into a zip archive followi: Use zipfile.ZipFile to compare namelist() sets between actual and expected zips; file list must match exactly before checking contents.

For non-PDF files inside the zip, compare raw bytes directly; for PDF files use a fuzzy text-content comparison (e.g., extract text and check similarity ratio) rather than byte equality, since PDF metadata/timestamps may differ.
The zip archive name itself is part of the submission requirement; verify the output path/filename matches the spec derived from the instruction document.
When the task reads requirements from a .docx file, the key variables are: which files to include, what to name the zip, and where to save it — all three must be verified independently.
save web page primary content to Word do: Use python-docx Document() to extract paragraph texts from the saved .docx and compare against expected content using fuzzy string matching (fuzz.ratio) after collapsing whitespace, since exact whitespace/blank-line differences are common when scraping and saving web content.

When verifying scraped web content saved to .docx, check that the document contains the expected section range (start heading present, excluded section heading absent) rather than exact character-level equality, as minor formatting differences are expected.
compare_docx_files with fuzzy_match=True and ignore_blanks=True is the appropriate metric family for this feature class; similarity threshold rather than exact match should be used.
capture terminal screenshot and save as: Use easyocr (compare_image_text metric) to verify screenshot content by OCR-extracting text from the saved PNG; the image may arrive as an X11 screen dump (.xwd) requiring conversion before OCR — handle PIL, custom X11 reader, and netpbm fallback chains

When verifying a terminal screenshot, check that expected command text appears anywhere in the OCR-extracted string (substring match), since OCR may misread characters (e.g., 'ls' vs '1s') — use multiple alternative target strings with 'or' conjunction
The compare_image_text metric accepts a rule dict with type='text' and a target string; it returns 1 if the target is a substring of all OCR-extracted text joined by spaces
enhance image brightness and save as PNG: Use PIL to compute mean brightness of both the output and reference images (e.g., via ImageStat or converting to grayscale and averaging pixel values); verify output brightness is strictly greater than the original.

After brightness normalization (scale both images to the same target mean brightness), compare structural similarity via MSE or SSIM to confirm the image content/structure is preserved despite the brightness change.

The check_brightness_decrease_and_structure_sim pattern is reusable: normalize both images to a common brightness level, then run an MSE-based structure check with a small threshold (e.g., 0.03–0.15) to distinguish brightness edits from content corruption.
convert image file to PDF: Use PyMuPDF (fitz) to extract embedded images from both the result and reference PDFs, then compare them with perceptual hashing (e.g., imagehash.phash); a hash difference below a small threshold (≈5) indicates the image content was preserved correctly during conversion.
Check that the output PDF contains the same number of embedded images as the reference PDF before doing any content comparison — mismatched counts should score 0.

When the PDF embeds the image directly (rather than rendering it as page content), fitz page.get_images() + extract_image() reliably retrieves the raw bytes for comparison; be aware that some conversion tools render the image as page pixels instead of embedding it, which would yield zero images from this method.
edit image per document instructions and: Use SSIM (structural similarity index) on grayscale versions of the result and reference images; resize both to the smaller dimension before comparison to handle minor size discrepancies.

When instructions are in a document on the Desktop, parse the document to extract transformation parameters (crop, rotate, resize, color adjustments, filters, etc.) before verifying the output image reflects those changes.
Compare images at the pixel/structural level rather than metadata; JPEG re-encoding introduces minor artifacts, so use a similarity threshold rather than exact equality.

The compare_images metric converts both images to grayscale and resizes to the smaller image's dimensions before SSIM calculation — account for this when the task involves color-specific edits (hue/saturation changes may not be distinguishable in grayscale SSIM).
populate email recipient fields from spr: Use check_accessibility_tree with CSS selectors targeting address-pill elements inside MsgHeadersToolbar's To field; each recipient email appears as a label with class 'pill-label' whose name attribute contains the address string

The accessibility tree selector pattern for Thunderbird compose/draft To-field pills is: tool-bar[attr|id=MsgHeadersToolbar] label[name=To]~[attr|class='address-pill']>label[attr|class='pill-label'][name*='<email>']
Verify each expected recipient independently as a separate rule so partial completion is detectable (score multiplied per rule)
extract email attachment and save to dir: Use binary diff (e.g., shell `diff` or Python filecmp) between the extracted file and a reference copy to verify both file content and correct destination path; a non-empty diff output indicates failure
Check that the saved filename matches the naming pattern of sibling files in the target directory (e.g., consistent prefix/suffix/date format) by listing directory contents and applying a regex
save web-researched location/address dat: Use python-docx to read the saved .docx and extract all paragraph text; split on whitespace to get individual tokens for fuzzy matching against expected address strings.

Use fuzz.ratio (from rapidfuzz/fuzzywuzzy) to score each extracted token against a list of valid address variants; aggregate scores to handle partial or abbreviated address forms (e.g., with or without city/district prefix).

Address content may appear as one entry per paragraph or multiple entries per paragraph; splitting paragraph text on whitespace and scoring each chunk independently is more robust than whole-paragraph comparison.
The expected set should include both full-form (深圳市福田区…) and short-form (福田区…) variants of each address to tolerate either style of user entry.
extract subtitles from video file and sa: Run a validator script (pysrt or similar) against the output .srt file and compare its content/timing against a gold .srt reference; exact_match on the script's boolean output ('true\n') is the pattern used here
Use pysrt to parse both the candidate and gold .srt files, comparing subtitle count, timing entries, and text content rather than raw byte equality

The evaluator script is downloaded post-config and executed via vm_command_line; the script itself encapsulates the comparison logic, so focus on ensuring the .srt file exists at the expected path and is parseable
extract and merge code from web notebook: Use compare_python_pure_text-style normalization: expand tabs to 4 spaces, strip trailing whitespace, drop empty lines, and skip only shebang/coding-declaration lines at the file head before comparing against a gold file.
The metric does exact normalized string equality, so line order, indentation, and content must match precisely — fuzzy or partial-match metrics are not used here.

When extracting from notebook code cells, include inline # comments but exclude triple-quoted markdown docstrings and file-header metadata; the gold file encodes this boundary, so diffing against it reveals extraction errors.
Use splitlines() + rstrip() rather than full AST parsing for normalization, since the check is text-level not semantic.
rename files based on visual content ide: Verification runs a helper script on the VM that hashes each file's content and returns a JSON mapping hash→filename; use check_direct_json_object with expect_in_result=true to allow multiple acceptable name variants per image hash.

The evaluator script computes SHA-256 (or similar) hashes of the renamed files and maps them to their new filenames, so verification is content-based rather than path-based — the same image renamed differently still matches.
Acceptable filename lists should include bare name, name with extension, and case variants; the expect_in_result flag lets any one entry in the list satisfy the check.
When filenames may contain spaces (task explicitly forbids underscore substitution), ensure the comparison list includes space-containing variants alongside no-space variants.
edit MP3 ID3 metadata tags (title, artis: Use mutagen's EasyID3 to read ID3 tags from MP3 files; EasyID3(path).get(tag_name) returns a list, so join with comma before comparing to expected string values
EasyID3 exposes normalized lowercase tag keys (e.g., 'title', 'artist') regardless of the ID3 frame names used to write them, making it a reliable cross-tool verification interface
When verifying batch tag edits, check each file independently; a partial success (some files tagged, others not) will produce a fractional aggregate score since each file is evaluated separately
install LibreOffice extension (.oxt): Verify installation by grepping recursively under the LibreOffice uno_packages cache directory (e.g., ~/.config/libreoffice/4/user/uno_packages/cache/uno_packages/) for the extension's .oxt filename pattern using check_list with regex expect rules.

For extensions requiring a Java runtime (e.g., LanguageTool), also verify that an openjdk JRE or JDK package is installed by running 'apt list --installed' and checking its output with a regex like 'openjdk-\d+-(jre|jdk)'.
Use postconfig command steps to capture grep and apt output to cache files, then apply check_list with regex-based expect rules against those files.
install and apply GNOME desktop theme: Use `gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface gtk-theme` to read the active GTK theme; check its stdout for the expected theme name string using regex/pattern matching
Theme installation typically places files under ~/.themes/ or /usr/share/themes/; verifying the gsettings value is sufficient without checking filesystem presence
The check_list pattern matches each line of the gsettings output against expect/unexpect regex patterns — a theme name substring match (not exact equality) is enough to pass
set desktop wallpaper/background image: Use get_vm_wallpaper() controller method to retrieve the current wallpaper as bytes, then compare with a reference image using grayscale SSIM; a similarity score above a baseline threshold (accounting for resolution differences via resize-to-smaller) indicates correct wallpaper was set
When comparing wallpapers, resize both images to the smaller of the two sizes before SSIM comparison to handle resolution mismatches between the set wallpaper and the reference
A reference_base_result baseline can filter out near-matches that are structurally similar but not the correct image; score is normalized as (ssim - base) / (1 - base)
download file from GitHub repository to: Use diff_text_file (difflib.SequenceMatcher ratio) to compare the downloaded file against a reference; a ratio near 1.0 indicates correct content — useful for text/source files like .tex where exact content matters.

When the target file must be placed in a specific subdirectory path, verify both the file's existence at that exact path and its content similarity to the reference, since the task combines correct URL resolution, correct file selection (next undownloaded chapter), and correct save location.
open directory in file manager (Nautilus: Use wmctrl -lx output to check for org.gnome.Nautilus window with the target directory name in the window title; parse each line with regex matching WM_CLASS and title fields.
open directory in terminal (gnome-termin: Use wmctrl -lx output to check for gnome-terminal-server.Gnome-terminal window with the target working directory path in the title; the path may appear as ~/... shorthand.
open specific URLs in Chrome browser tab: Use the open_tabs_info getter (Playwright CDP) to retrieve all open tab URLs; compare against expected URL list using URL-aware equality (compare_urls handles trailing slashes, protocol variants); tab order may matter depending on the rule.
convert TXT files to EPUB format: Use compare_epub which calls process_epub to extract text files from the epub archive, then diff_text_file to compare content against a reference epub; the metric is the average similarity across paired text files.

An epub is a zip archive; process_epub likely unzips it and returns sorted content files (e.g., .xhtml/.html chapters); verify both structure (number of content files) and text similarity against a gold epub.
Accept case/underscore variants in the output filename (e.g., 'Title.epub', 'Title_.epub', 'title_.epub') when checking file existence on the VM.
The compare_epub metric returns a float in [0,1]; a threshold near 1.0 indicates correct content conversion, while 0 means the file is missing or empty.
compress image file to meet size constra: Use os.path.getsize() to verify the output file's byte size is strictly below the required max_size threshold; no image parsing needed for the size check alone.
When the task allows resizing as an alternative to quality reduction, only the final file size matters — verify size only, not specific dimensions or quality settings.
The vm_file getter copies the file locally before the metric runs; check_image_file_size simply calls os.path.getsize on the local copy and compares to rule['max_size'].
split and rearrange image sections via c: Use SSIM-based structural similarity (check_structure_sim pattern) to compare output PNG against a reference image; both images must have identical dimensions for a non-zero score.
Verify output image dimensions match the original (width × height unchanged after splitting and rejoining sections horizontally).

When checking section reordering correctness, compare pixel column strips of the output against expected column strips from the reference; SSIM on the full image captures both spatial structure and color ordering.
crop image and save as PNG file: Use PIL to open the output image and compare dimensions against expected crop geometry (e.g., height should equal original minus cropped fraction, width unchanged)
Use SSIM-based structural similarity (check_structure_sim pattern) to compare the cropped output against a reference image; both images must have identical sizes before SSIM is meaningful
When verifying percentage-based crops, derive expected pixel dimensions from the original image size rather than hardcoding values
download files from web into a local dir: Use compare_archive with file_type='pdf' to compare directory contents: first verify filenames match exactly (sorted listing equality), then compare PDF content pairwise using compare_pdfs; both filename set and content must match the gold archive.
When verifying downloaded PDFs, compare_pdfs is the appropriate comparison function; it handles PDF-specific content comparison beyond raw byte equality.
Archive-based evaluation zips the target folder then unpacks both pred and gold archives, so the directory structure and filenames inside the folder are what matter, not the zip name itself.
split document/book into multiple chapte: Use compare_archive with file_type='pdf' to compare a zip of produced chapter PDFs against a gold zip; filenames must match exactly (sorted comparison), so verify naming pattern matches the example chapter file provided in the task environment.

For PDF content comparison, the compare_pdfs function is used internally; ensure each split PDF contains only the pages belonging to its chapter — page count and text content per file are the key signals.

Archive comparison first checks that pred_files == gold_files (sorted filenames); a mismatch in naming or count immediately returns 0, so filename convention adherence is critical to verify before content.
populate spreadsheet with computed score: Use openpyxl/pandas sheet_data comparison (DataFrame.equals after rounding) to verify that score columns are correctly computed and written; load both result and gold xlsx with pd.ExcelFile and compare the target sheet as DataFrames, ensuring numeric score values match within a precision tolerance.
install application via package manager: Use `which <app>` via vm_command_line to confirm the binary is on PATH after installation; check that output includes the app name and excludes 'not found'.
For snap/apt/flatpak installs, `which` is the most reliable post-install check since it reflects PATH registration, not just package metadata.
configure GNOME power/session settings v: Use `gsettings get <schema> <key>` via vm_command_line to verify power/session settings; org.gnome.desktop.session idle-delay returns a uint32 value, org.gnome.settings-daemon.plugins.power idle-dim returns a boolean string — match exact output format including type prefix (e.g., 'uint32 0') and trailing newline.
configure GNOME favorite apps (dock/task: Use `gsettings get org.gnome.shell favorite-apps` (with DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS set for the user session) to retrieve the current favorites list as a Python-evaluable string; eval() it to get a list and compare as a set against expected .desktop entries.
Check both list length and set equality to ensure no extra or missing entries remain after the edit.
configure GNOME notification settings vi: Use `gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.notifications show-banners` to verify Do Not Disturb / notification banner state; the value is a boolean string ('true'/'false') including a trailing newline in command output.
set system audio volume via PulseAudio: Use `pactl list sinks` and parse the Volume line to extract the percentage; `pulseaudio --start` may be needed before querying to ensure the daemon is running
The `pactl set-sink-volume` command accepts percentage strings (e.g., '100%'); verify by re-querying the sink volume after setting it
Volume percentage can be extracted with awk/sed from the `pactl list sinks` output; compare the numeric value against the expected level
restore file from Trash to original/targ: Use a vm_command_line getter with a shell test (`[ -f <path> ]`) to confirm the file exists at the expected restored location; exact_match against 'File exists.\n' is the standard pattern.
Check that the file is no longer present in the Trash directory (e.g., ~/.local/share/Trash/files/) as a complementary assertion when needed.
rename directory: Use a shell command via vm_command_line to test directory existence (e.g., `[ -d <path> ] && echo exists`) and exact_match against the expected output string.
set system timezone: Run `timedatectl status` and parse the 'Time zone' line; check that the UTC offset field (e.g., `+0000`) matches the target offset — the evaluator parses line index 3 of the output and checks the trailing offset string.
configure GNOME text scaling and accessi: Use gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface text-scaling-factor to verify text scaling; parse the float and compare against a minimum threshold using bc -l for floating-point comparison in shell.

Use gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.a11y.applications screen-magnifier-enabled and org.gnome.desktop.a11y.magnifier mag-factor together; both must be checked (magnifier enabled AND factor above threshold) to confirm zoom is active.
Both text-scaling-factor and screen magnifier are valid alternative approaches to enlarging text; evaluators should accept either path succeeding (OR conjunction).
configure GNOME screensaver/lock setting: Use `gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.screensaver <key>` to verify lock-related settings; key families include lock-enabled, lock-delay, idle-activation-enabled under org.gnome.desktop.screensaver and org.gnome.desktop.session.
persist terminal window size across rebo: Use get_vm_terminal_output after opening a new terminal and running 'stty size' to verify rows/columns; check_include_exclude against the expected 'rows cols' string is the right metric family.

Persistent terminal size is typically set via 'stty rows C cols R' in ~/.bashrc, ~/.profile, or a terminal profile config; verify the relevant config file contains the stty command or equivalent profile setting rather than just checking the current session.
recursively find and copy files by exten: Use list_directory / get_vm_directory_tree on the destination directory and compare the set of filenames against expected filenames; count equality is a necessary pre-check before set equality to avoid false positives when duplicates exist.

The evaluator only checks the flat contents of the destination directory (not subdirectory structure), so verify that all matching files from nested source folders are flattened into the single target directory.
When filenames contain URL-encoded or percent-encoded characters, compare using the exact encoded string as it appears in the filesystem.
create SSH user with specific home direc: Use `getent passwd <username>` to verify user existence and home directory (field 6); use `stat -c "%A"` on the home directory to check write permissions; verify password correctness programmatically via an `expect` script that attempts SSH/login with the given credentials rather than reading /etc/shadow directly
copy files matching glob pattern preserv: Use a shell script (eval.sh) executed via vm_command_line to verify: check that matched files exist under the target directory with the same relative path structure as in the source tree; the eval script typically uses find + path comparison or diff-style checks to confirm hierarchy preservation.
text processing and file content transfo: Use vm_command_line to read the output file and verify line-by-line content; a shell script (eval.sh) is often used to check exact file contents, so running it and checking for a success string is the primary verification pattern.

When the task involves appending/prepending to lines, check that every line in the output file ends (or starts) with the expected string, including edge cases like the last line without a trailing newline.
compress and organize files by modificat: Use shell commands (find with -mtime, ls -la, stat) via vm_command_line to verify file timestamps, archive presence, and directory structure; check that old files are compressed (e.g., zip/tar) in the target subdirectory and newer files are moved (not copied) to the other subdirectory
Verify that files are moved (not present in original location) and that the archive is valid/extractable using shell commands like unzip -t or tar -tzf
Check modification time thresholds carefully: find -mtime +N finds files modified more than N days ago; off-by-one errors are common when interpreting '30 days ago'
count lines of files by extension recurs: Use `get_vm_terminal_output` to capture terminal stdout; verify the output contains the expected numeric result using `check_include_exclude` with include/exclude string rules

Common commands for this task family: `find . -name '*.ext' | xargs wc -l` or `find . -name '*.ext' -exec cat {} + | wc -l`; the total line count appears in terminal output and can be matched as a substring
recursively change file permissions (chm: Use `find . -type f` to enumerate regular files and check their permissions with `stat` or `os.stat`; verify the octal mode matches the target (e.g., 0o644) for every file, not just a sample
A shell eval script approach (running `find`+`stat` in a loop) is the canonical way to verify bulk permission changes; the result string can be matched against a success/failure message
Distinguish `-type f` (regular files only) from `-type d` (directories) — permission tasks often apply only to one type, so the evaluator script should filter accordingly
copy file to multiple target directories: Use a shell script or vm_command_line to check file existence in each target directory; the check_include_exclude pattern with per-directory success/failure messages is a reliable approach for multi-destination copy verification.
